1. Understand Calorie Deficit:
The key to weight loss is consuming fewer calories than your body needs. Consume 200–300 calories less than your daily expenditure.

2. Cut Sugar & Refined Carbs:
Significantly reduce sweets, cold drinks, fast food, and white rice. Instead, opt for brown rice, oats, or whole-wheat bread.

3. Increase Protein & Fiber:
Include adequate protein (eggs, chicken, fish, lentils) and fiber-rich vegetables in every meal to keep you full longer.

4. Drink Water Rightly:
Drink 3–4 liters of water daily. Drink a glass of water 30 minutes before meals to prevent overeating.

5. Regular Moderate Exercise:
Exercise or brisk walk for 30–40 minutes at least 5 days a week to boost metabolism and burn fat.

1. Calorie Surplus Diet:
To gain weight, eat 300–500 calories more than your daily requirement. Focus on nutrient-dense foods instead of junk food.

2. Nutrient-Rich & High-Calorie Foods:
Eat calorie-dense foods like almonds, cashews, peanut butter, raisins, dates, eggs, whole milk, bananas, and ghee.

3. Frequent Meals:
Eat 5–6 smaller, nutritious meals instead of 3 large meals. Snack on nuts, fruits, or puddings in between.

4. No Water Before Meals:
Avoid drinking water right before or during meals, as it fills your stomach and reduces your appetite.

5. Strength Training:
Do push-ups, squats, or light gym work to build muscle mass rather than just gaining unhealthy fat.

1. Balanced Diet:
Fill half your plate with veggies and fruits, one-quarter with protein, and one-quarter with complex carbs. Eat at least one seasonal fruit daily.

2. Adequate & Deep Sleep:
7 to 8 hours of uninterrupted sleep is essential. Poor sleep disrupts hormonal balance, causing unexpected weight changes.

3. Manage Stress:
High stress slows down metabolism. Practice deep breathing exercises or meditation for 10–15 minutes daily.

4. Avoid Processed & Trans-Fats:
Packaged foods, deep-fried items, and excessive salt harm your heart. Always prefer fresh, home-cooked food.

5. Stay Active:
Avoid sitting continuously. Stand up or walk for 2 minutes every hour. Choose stairs over elevators whenever possible.
